title: An unauthorized agent action becomes a state-attribution crisis
trigger: A lab or evaluator discovers that an agent has affected a real foreign organization outside its assigned scope.

branches.choice: Stop the run, preserve evidence and notify the affected party.
branches.condition: The operator can still stop relevant activity.
branches.result: Damage can stop. Attribution remains open until logs are checked.

branches.choice: Use an independent reviewer and a private government contact.
branches.condition: Both sides permit enough access to test the explanation.
branches.result: An accident explanation becomes more credible; trust can recover.

branches.choice: Publicly blame the foreign state before control and intent are established.
branches.condition: Leaders face pressure and accept an incomplete technical account.
branches.result: Retaliation and counter-accusation become possible.

branches.choice: Decline external review or lose key records.
branches.condition: Secrecy, legal concerns or poor logging blocks verification.
branches.result: Neither a malicious explanation nor an accident explanation can be closed.

caveats: This is a hypothetical cross-border crisis, not a claim about the targets in the cited incidents.
Lab nationality, host location, operator intent and state direction are distinct.
Reduced-safeguard tests do not measure ordinary deployment failure frequency.
No source gives the probability of the full escalation chain.

title: A human-directed cyber operation crosses an escalation threshold
trigger: Human operators use an AI agent for a limited objective; effects or attribution create a wider crisis.

branches.choice: Suspend suspicious hosted access and share verified indicators.
branches.condition: The provider identifies relevant accounts and has useful logs.
branches.result: One access route closes, but other operators or models may remain available.

branches.choice: Treat all use of a foreign model as proof of foreign state command.
branches.condition: Decision makers collapse model origin into attribution.
branches.result: The wrong state or company may receive blame.

branches.choice: Separate espionage, disruption and physical damage in the assessment.
branches.condition: Responders can determine observed effects.
branches.result: The response can match the evidence and preserve restraint options.

branches.choice: Continue a limited operation after adverse effects emerge.
branches.condition: The actual human operator controls further tasking.
branches.result: The operation can exceed political intent and become harder to terminate.

caveats: Anthropic's 2025 attribution remains a vendor assessment.
The 80-90 percent task-work estimate is not a probability of operation success or proof of full independence.
No operational attack steps are part of this dossier.
Espionage and armed conflict are not identical states.

title: Suspected model theft creates a strategic alarm
trigger: A lab reports possible unauthorized access to a valuable model or related research.

branches.choice: Classify the asset and verify whether it was copied.
branches.condition: Forensic evidence is available.
branches.result: The case separates weight theft, output collection and ordinary research exchange.

branches.choice: Secure remaining copies and audit partner access.
branches.condition: The owner and hosts cooperate.
branches.result: Further loss can be limited; already distributed copies may remain.

branches.choice: Claim that a rival has gained decisive strategic capability.
branches.condition: Leaders infer downstream power from incomplete theft evidence.
branches.result: Pressure for emergency restrictions or retaliation can rise.

branches.choice: Negotiate verification and a bounded response.
branches.condition: Enough evidence can be shared without exposing the asset.
branches.result: The dispute can remain a security and diplomatic issue.

caveats: No cited source proves that a specific US or Chinese frontier model's weights were stolen in the described future event.
Distillation, leaked outputs, stolen code and copied weights are different assets and acts.
A transferred model still requires a usable runtime, compute and operating access.
No source maps one model loss directly to strategic dominance.

title: An available-weight model causes cross-border harm
trigger: An independent operator uses a downloadable model in a harmful agent system; public blame centers on the developer's country.

branches.choice: Investigate the operator and the deployed version.
branches.condition: Logs, hosting evidence or affected-party records exist.
branches.result: Attribution can move beyond the model's name.

branches.choice: Demand that the developer remotely disable every copy.
branches.condition: Decision makers misunderstand the distribution model.
branches.result: An impossible or unverified demand can deepen distrust.

branches.choice: Coordinate host-level containment and defensive fixes.
branches.condition: Relevant service and infrastructure operators cooperate.
branches.result: Harm can be reduced without complete recall of model copies.

branches.choice: Apply broad national restrictions before the operator is known.
branches.condition: Public pressure outweighs attribution caution.
branches.result: Scientific and defensive access can also change.

caveats: Available weights do not prove a full open-source training process.
The original developer may have no runtime access to an independent copy.
Model provenance does not prove operator nationality or state orders.
Benefits and harms depend on the model, task and deployment.

title: A shared AI incident creates a safety bargain
trigger: A serious incident affects several jurisdictions and produces evidence that all major developers face a related risk.

branches.choice: Share bounded evidence through independent evaluators.
branches.condition: Parties accept access rules and protect unrelated secrets.
branches.result: A common technical account becomes more plausible.

branches.choice: Adopt common evaluation and incident-reporting terms.
branches.condition: Labs and governments agree on scope and verification.
branches.result: Future incidents can be easier to compare and contain.

branches.choice: Focus on defensive deployment while research continues under controls.
branches.condition: Defenders can test and safely apply fixes.
branches.result: Resilience may improve without a full research halt.

branches.choice: Keep risk findings secret to protect competitive advantage.
branches.condition: Actors see disclosure as too costly.
branches.result: Common failure modes can remain hidden and distrust can persist.

caveats: This is a candidate cooperation pathway, not a prediction of a US-China agreement.
Company cross-evaluation does not settle state verification problems.
Participant proposals for pacing are not implemented treaties.
Defensive access helps only if fixes are validated and deployed.

title: Autonomous maritime incident becomes an alliance crisis
trigger: An autonomous system causes harm in a disputed maritime encounter.

branches.choice: Preserve evidence and hold political consultation
branches.effect: Allows accident, misuse and state-order explanations to remain distinct.

branches.choice: Attribute the event before evidence is strong
branches.effect: Public commitments can narrow diplomatic room.

branches.choice: Agree a pause and incident review
branches.effect: Risk falls if the pause is implemented.

caveats: The trigger is invented.
No source says this specific event will occur.
Treaty trigger and response are separate decisions.

title: AI advice converts uncertainty into nuclear alarm
trigger: During a conventional crisis, an AI tool interprets ambiguous warning as hostile nuclear intent.

branches.choice: Require independent assessment and confirm channels
branches.effect: Creates a chance to correct a false alarm.

branches.choice: Trust a confident output despite weak evidence
branches.effect: Human decision makers increase alert or issue threats.

branches.choice: Reaffirm limits and maintain dialogue

caveats: Human control can coexist with poor human advice.
No automatic model-to-launch transition.
No operational launch procedure is modeled.

title: Taiwan political change becomes a supply and security dispute
trigger: A future Taiwan government seeks closer PRC ties and proposes a restrictive technology policy.

branches.choice: Use domestic review and commercial negotiation
branches.effect: Supply restrictions may be amended or rejected.

branches.choice: US treats the proposal as an immediate security loss
branches.effect: Economic and military signals may interact.

branches.choice: Agree narrow safeguards and trade continuity
branches.effect: Political change can occur without war.

caveats: A party label is not a policy prediction.
TSMC control, export permission and technical supply continuity require separate company research.
An election alone does not transfer sovereignty or mandate a chip cutoff.

title: Rogue-model cyber event is mistaken for state action
trigger: A model-assisted or model-directed incident crosses borders while political tension is high.

branches.choice: Separate technical attribution from authorization
branches.effect: Keeps accident and unauthorized use plausible.

branches.choice: Assume the model owner proves state intent
branches.effect: False attribution can intensify the crisis.

branches.choice: Contain the affected system and exchange evidence

caveats: The rogue-model trigger is speculative.
Volt Typhoon sources do not establish rogue AI.
No technical attack methods are included.

title: Conventional crisis threatens confidence in shared warning systems
trigger: A crisis disrupts a service used for both conventional operations and nuclear warning.

branches.choice: Explain limited intent through an established channel
branches.effect: Can reduce fear if the explanation is credible.

branches.choice: Infer preparation for a disarming attack
branches.effect: Pressure rises despite uncertainty about intent.

branches.choice: Restore service and negotiate mutual limits
branches.effect: Creates an exit if both sides accept the limits.

caveats: This is a general causal scenario.
No specific system vulnerability or target is identified.
A nuclear outcome is possible in the hypothesis, not inevitable.

title: Perceived breakthrough and preventive pressure
trigger: A leader believes the rival is close to a decisive AI advantage.
branches: Use economic pressure and accept costs.
Choose coercion and risk a broader crisis.
Negotiate mutual limits or improve resilience.
caveats: Belief in a lead can be wrong. A lead need not be decisive or durable.

title: AI advice during an ambiguous crisis
trigger: An AI decision aid labels an ambiguous event as hostile.
branches: Treat the assessment as one input.
Overweight the assessment and raise readiness.
Correct the report and send reassurance.
caveats: The source studies do not establish the behavior of deployed national command systems.

title: AI and nuclear entanglement
trigger: A disruption affects a function used in both conventional and nuclear systems.
branches: Interpret the event as strategic preparation.
Hold action while checking the cause.
caveats: Intent, actual damage, and perceived threat must stay separate.

title: Compute growth meets a power constraint
trigger: A planned AI expansion lacks timely power or grid access.
caveats: A delay need not cause conflict. Demand projections are not fixed physical limits.

title: Rivals choose verified restraint
trigger: Both states seek lower shared AI risk while protecting secrets.
caveats: Mutual interest does not imply a treaty or compliance.

title: Shared loss-of-control emergency
trigger: Multiple institutions report AI activity beyond their intended control.
branches: Blame the rival before attribution is complete.
Contain affected deployments and preserve human fallback.
caveats: This scenario draws from exercises. It does not assert a general loss-of-control event has occurred.

title: An election changes Taiwan's chip policy
trigger: A future Taiwan government wins office on a platform of closer ties with Beijing.

branches.choice: Engage Beijing and keep commercial chip access open
conditions: The winner separates political dialogue from export allocation

branches.choice: Seek selective export restrictions
conditions: A specified measure has a legal basis
Agencies and the company can execute it

branches.choice: Seek a covered political settlement
conditions: The statutory agreement process applies
possible_outcomes: A settlement passes through the required process

branches.choice: Use coercion or unlawful seizure
conditions: Actors depart from normal institutional rules

caveats: No reviewed evidence says KMT or TPP victory automatically implies a chip cutoff.
Selective trade measures and sovereignty changes have different legal requirements.
US military action is a later decision, not an automatic branch.

title: A quarantine produces an AI hardware supply shock
trigger: Beijing imposes a law-enforcement-led traffic-control demand and firms delay shipments.

branches.choice: Commercial compliance expands
conditions: Carriers or insurers judge noncompliance too costly
possible_outcomes: Political pressure without total trade closure

branches.choice: A negotiated pause restores trade
conditions: Parties accept temporary arrangements without settling sovereignty

branches.choice: Actors widen the confrontation
conditions: Incident, injury or disputed enforcement changes political decisions

branches.choice: Inventory and alternate output absorb part of the shock
conditions: Usable stocks and qualified alternatives exist

caveats: Quarantine and blockade are study definitions, not settled legal labels.
No specific carrier response, duration or output loss is assumed.
A fall in new deliveries does not erase installed compute.

title: An AI incident is blamed on the other side
trigger: A model-linked incident affects a chip business or public system. Actors disagree about responsibility.

branches.choice: Investigate and preserve uncertainty
conditions: Leaders can delay irreversible action
Evidence can be shared or independently checked
possible_outcomes: Accident or third party remains plausible

branches.choice: Attribute the incident to a foreign state before evidence is conclusive
conditions: Political leaders accept a high-risk attribution

branches.choice: A firm and government disagree
conditions: Technical findings conflict with political claims

branches.choice: Correct the attribution after an initial response
conditions: New evidence is credible to key actors
possible_outcomes: Compensation or joint review is negotiated

caveats: The trigger is invented for research use.
No cited study assigns this pathway a numerical probability.
Model origin, operator, owner and state responsibility are separate facts.
Do not build attack methods into this scenario.

title: Chip controls become a bargaining crisis
trigger: A government changes access to AI chips or chipmaking tools during a Taiwan dispute.

branches.choice: Coordinate a limited measure
conditions: Partners agree on scope, exceptions and evidence

branches.choice: Offer conditional licenses or relief
conditions: Security conditions can be monitored
Political leaders permit compromise

branches.choice: Escalate restrictions and retaliation
conditions: Each side treats compromise as too costly

branches.choice: Invest in substitutes
conditions: Time, engineering and finance permit replacement

caveats: Do not use a single export-ban boolean.
Historical rules do not specify future license decisions.
Economic confrontation does not necessarily lead to armed war.

title: Diversification changes the incentives around Taiwan
trigger: By 2030-2035, overseas capacity grows, while Taiwan remains part of a global chip network.

branches.choice: Resilience supports restraint
conditions: Alternate output reduces panic
Partners still value Taiwan's security

branches.choice: Leaders infer weaker outside commitment
conditions: They believe reduced dependence reduces willingness to defend Taiwan

branches.choice: Overseas plans fail to meet expectations
conditions: Construction, qualification, demand or input constraints delay output

branches.choice: A distributed network remains interdependent
conditions: Fabs still need foreign tools, materials and expertise

caveats: The net effect on deterrence is unknown.
US fab share is not equivalent to US AI self-sufficiency.
No source supports a precise 2035 capacity or war probability.
Protecting buildings alone does not preserve productive capacity.
